definition: A pack's formula for one dimension of the house — the crown as a reduced entablature, the chair rail at the pedestal cap, the casing at a sixth of the opening's width. Where the sources do not settle a figure, the rule says so.
more: A rule reads the module and the measures of the building it is worked for — ceiling height, door width, storey height. It may also say it was calibrated for certain rooms, that it applies only to one kind of wall, or that it is designed to fail informatively when two dimensions of a room cannot both be classical.
